best_for: Teams that run their own Rocket.Chat server, or belong to one, and want it in a desktop window with native notifications and several workspaces side by side.
description:
Rocket.Chat Desktop is the official desktop app for Rocket.Chat, a team chat platform that organizations run on servers they control. The app is built with Electron. Rocket.Chat says national agencies, classified programs and EU institutions use the platform for their most sensitive work.

What you get depends on your workspace's server. Rocket.Chat lists AI search across the rooms you can access and thread summaries, with answers drawn only from what each person may see and run on models the organization picks inside its own network. A bridge can keep colleagues on Microsoft Teams in the same conversation. On the desktop, closing the window can hide the app in the tray, minimize it, or quit.

points.title: A client, not the server
points.text: The desktop app connects to Rocket.Chat workspaces that someone already runs. It doesn't host chat by itself.

points.title: Several workspaces in one window
points.text: Add more than one workspace to the sidebar and switch between them without signing out. Video calls open in a window inside the app.

points.title: Server plans in brief
points.text: The free Starter plan is self-hosted and covers up to 50 users. Larger Commercial, Government and Defense plans are quote-only, with no prices published.

points.title: IT can preset it
points.text: Admins can preload workspaces with `servers.json`, lock settings such as auto-update with `overridden-settings.json`, and install silently with the .exe or MSI.

points.title: Linux gets less
points.text: Quick reply from notifications works on Windows and macOS only. Linux builds are x64 only, and the Flatpak listed here is not marked verified by Flathub.

points.title: Install options
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 84 versions, with per-user or all-users installers for x86, x64 and Arm64 on Windows 10 or later. macOS has a universal disk image for macOS 12 or later, current release only. The app is open source under MIT.
